headline: Fashion is nonverbal communication—clothes signal identity, status, and belonging before we speak
universal_truth: Everything we choose communicates something; there is no neutral presentation
fun_facts: Studies show wearing formal clothes makes people think more abstractly and feel more powerful
Purple was so expensive in ancient Rome that only emperors could wear it—clothing as law
School uniforms were invented partly to prevent visible class differences between students
discussion_questions: What does your clothing communicate about you?
Why do different contexts require different dress codes?
Can you dress 'neutrally,' or does every choice send a message?

hook.script: Before you speak a word, your clothes have already spoken. They announce your profession, your tribe, your status, your mood. Every choice—formal or casual, colorful or plain—sends a message. Fashion is language without words.

cliff.script: We all wear clothes, but most of us don't consciously think about what they communicate. How do clothes actually convey meaning to others?

options.text: Clothes signal group membership, social status, and intentions through culturally shared symbols and associations
options.response: Yes. We've learned what different clothes 'mean'—suits mean business, uniforms mean authority, casual means relaxation. These are cultural codes we all read unconsciously.

options.text: Clothes express personal style and individual creativity
options.response: Personal expression matters, but even 'individual' style uses shared cultural vocabulary...

fact1.title: Status Signals
fact1.script: Throughout history, clothing marked social rank. Sumptuary laws restricted who could wear what. Purple for emperors. Silk for nobles. Today's status symbols are subtler—designer labels, quality materials—but still communicate hierarchy.

fact2.title: Tribal Uniforms
fact2.script: We dress to belong. Business suits, punk leather, hippie tie-dye, athletic wear—each is a tribal uniform saying 'I'm one of you.' Even dressing 'differently' signals membership in the tribe of nonconformists.

fact3.title: Clothes Change Thinking
fact3.script: Studies show wearing formal clothes makes people think more abstractly. Wearing a doctor's coat improves attention. Clothes don't just communicate to others—they change how we feel and think. What you wear affects who you become.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Everything we choose communicates something. Clothing teaches that there is no neutral presentation—even trying not to send a message sends a message. Choose consciously.

outro.script: That's Day 161. Tomorrow, we'll discover why play matters. Until then, notice what your clothes are saying about you—and whether that matches what you intend.

growTrack.title: Clothing Audit - What Are You Saying?
growTrack.learning_objective: Increase awareness of clothing as communication
growTrack.activity: Look at what you're wearing right now. What message does it send? What assumptions would a stranger make? Does your clothing match what you want to communicate? Dress deliberately tomorrow—choose clothes that say what you intend.
